subject: Authorization playbook request and retention SLA
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Ari Becker <ari@finatrix.com>, Finatrix Security <security@finatrix.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Authorization playbook request and retention SLA

Hi Ari / Finatrix team,

Great conversation this morning — thanks for walking through your platform and risk model. Quick recap from Redwood and a list of clarifying questions so we can build a focused authorization + retention proposal.

High-level Finatrix asks we captured:
- PII handling: classification at ingestion; ability to redact or tokenise PII on demand.
- Data residency: all customer content and logs must remain in us-east (single-region).
- Retention: customer-content retention policy options (30/90/180 days) plus long-term audit storage for transaction metadata up to 7 years for regulated products.
- Logging & audit: Admin/operator logs must be immutable and retained for >=365 days; access logs must contain actor, reason, ticket id.
- Support access: scoped, least-privilege with JIT (time-limited), multi-step approval for break-glass, full recording of session activity.
- RBAC: role separation between support, ops, and engineering; ability to create custom role sets.

Clarifying questions for you (so we can scope the proposal):
1) Which data classes require the 7-year retention? (e.g., transaction traces vs. full content)
2) Do you require live redaction at inference time, or is post-ingest tokenisation acceptable?
3) For break-glass approvals, is a single security approver OK, or do you need a two-person approval pattern?
4) Any specific evidence artifacts you want in the SOC2 snapshot? (policy vs. operational runbooks vs. sample logs)

Next steps from Redwood (proposed timeline):
- We’ll produce a 1-page Authorization Playbook (RBAC diagram, support JIT flow, break-glass SOP) — owner: Vanessa (deliver in 3 business days).
- We’ll produce retention options and estimated cost delta matrix (owner: Logan, 4 business days).
- We’ll attach a SOC2 evidence snapshot and an initial support matrix for your review.

Attachments: support_matrix.xlsx (stub), soc2-evidence-request.pdf (stub)

Would you prefer a focused security deep-dive (30–45m) or a wider ops+security session?

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Ari Becker <ari@finatrix.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Finatrix Security <security@finatrix.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Authorization playbook request and retention SLA

Ben — thanks for the recap. Correct on all points; a few clarifications so your playbook aligns to our control objectives:

1) 7-year retention is required only for financial transaction metadata (audit trails). Customer full-text content can be shorter (we typically request 180 days, but 90 is acceptable for lower-risk flows).
2) Redaction: we want the option for both. Prefer live redaction for any PII-containing fields (SSN, bank account) during ingestion for production streams; tokenisation is acceptable for logs and non-real-time flows.
3) Break-glass: Finatrix's policy is two-person approval whenever customer production data is accessed by vendor support (one security approver + one engineering manager).
4) SOC2 snapshot: we need evidence of access reviews, logging retention policies, and a sample admin-access audit for the last 90 days.

One more operational constraint: any support session must be initiated from an open ticket in our system and include the ticket ID in the session metadata. Also, MFA and SSO are mandatory for vendor accounts.

Attach: I’ve added our internal support matrix and a short questionnaire. Please send your playbook and the SOC2 items to procurement@finatrix.com and security@finatrix.com once ready.

We prefer a security deep-dive first (45m) — Thurs or Fri next week works.

—Ari
Ari Becker
Director, Security Engineering
Finatrix

On Tue, Nov 16, 2026 at 09:12 AM Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com> wrote:
> (See above)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: ben@redwood.com, marissa@redwood.com, logan@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-16T14:20:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Authorization playbook request and retention SLA (internal notes)

Internal notes / proposed positions before the deep-dive:

- Residency: Offer single-region us-east as standard for Finatrix (no-replication), with Dedicated VPC as optional paid add-on for stricter isolation.
- Retention tiers: propose 30/90/180 day content tiers; separate audit-store add-on (7 years) for transaction metadata only. Include cost delta per TB.
- RBAC: Redwood can provide role templates: support_readonly, support_jit_temp (scoped), ops_admin (no data exfil permissions). Add ability to create custom roles via Console API.
- Support access / break-glass: propose the following minimal flow:
  * Customer opens ticket -> vendor support requests JIT session -> Customer security (or delegated approver) confirms via ticket + email -> session is granted for N hours and recorded to immutable audit logs -> session terminates automatically; all steps logged and exported.
  * For break-glass on PII, require 2 approvers as Finatrix requires.
- Logging: Admin and access logs retained 365 days by default; raw request logs for content retention follow customer content tier.

Ownership:
- Marissa: draft Authorization Playbook (RBAC + JIT flow + break-glass SOP) — 3 business days.
- Logan: retention cost matrix and sample console screenshots for role creation API — 4 business days.
- Ben: coordinate scheduling for Thurs/Fri deep-dive and handle procurement contact.

Flagging items we may want pre-prepared for the call:
- Short recording of a JIT session (sanitized) and an export of an audit log entry.
- A SOC2 evidence packet with redacted artifacts (access review logs, policies).

If everyone agrees, I’ll assemble a one-slide agenda for the Finatrix deep-dive and circulate.

-Vanessa
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Ari Becker <ari@finatrix.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Authorization playbook request and retention SLA

Ari — thanks for the quick clarifications. We’ll proceed with the plan and aim to have the initial deliverables sent ahead of the deep-dive:

What we’ll deliver before the call (expected EOD Wed):
- Authorization Playbook (RBAC diagram, JIT & break-glass SOP) — Vanessa owner.
- Retention & cost delta matrix (30/90/180 + 7yr audit-store) — Logan owner.
- Redacted SOC2 evidence packet (access reviews, sample logs) — Marissa owner (PDF).
- Support matrix (stub) and proposed ticket-ID gating for JIT sessions — attached in follow-up.

Pre-call asks for Finatrix: please confirm your preferred deep-dive slot (Thu 11/19 11:00–11:45 PT or Fri 11/20 09:00–09:45 PT) and identify the approver(s) who will represent Finatrix security during the session.

We’ll send the attachments to procurement@finatrix.com and security@finatrix.com as requested. If there are any changes to the two-approver break-glass requirement, flag it now so we can include it in the playbook.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
